record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: In short-term operational harvesting, an approximately 400-hectare harvest area must be assigned to skidders, cable towers, and access roads so that timber cells can be reached and hauled efficiently. The open question is how to formulate and solve this machinery-and-road location problem exactly, rather than heuristically, for large-scale instances where the model combines plant-location-style assignment decisions with fixed-charge network-flow road-building decisions.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 How can we solve the equipment location problem in an exact formulation for large-scale instances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an operational forest harvesting area of roughly 400 hectares partitioned into a finite set C of timber cells, each with a known harvestable volume. Available extraction resources consist of:
(i) a set S of candidate skidder locations (each with a setup/fixed cost, a reachable subset of cells, and per-unit-volume operating cost),
(ii) a set T of candidate cable-tower locations (each with a fixed installation cost, a cable-reach subset of cells subject to slope/length constraints, and per-unit-volume operating cost),
(iii) a directed road network graph G = (N, A), where N includes all candidate landings (skidder/tower positions) and exit nodes, A is a set of potential road segments each having a fixed construction cost and a per-unit-volume haul cost, and where existing roads are modeled as arcs with zero construction cost.

Decisions to be made:
• For each candidate skidder s ∈ S and tower t ∈ T, a binary opening decision.
• For each cell c ∈ C, an assignment to exactly one opened skidder or tower whose reachable subset contains c.
• For each arc a ∈ A, a binary build decision plus a continuous flow variable carrying timber volume from active landings to exit nodes; flow conservation must hold at every node, and arcs can carry positive flow only if built (fixed-charge network flow).

The objective is to minimize the total cost (fixed equipment-opening costs + fixed road-building costs + variable operating/haul costs) subject to all cells being assigned and all assigned volume being routed to exit nodes through built arcs.

Problem: Provide an exact mixed-integer programming formulation, together with an exact solution algorithm (e.g., based on decomposition, valid inequalities, or branch-and-cut/price), that is provably capable of solving large-scale instances of this combined plant-location and fixed-charge network-flow road-building problem to optimality within practical computing time.
artifact.status_search_result: No published exact algorithm for the combined skidder/cable-tower location with fixed-charge road-building model at the ~400-ha operational scale appears in the literature; existing approaches remain heuristic or restricted to smaller instances. The problem is listed as an explicit open problem in the originating survey, and no subsequent resolution was found.
